answer: Bond depreciation makes hoarded identities bleed value, so forgery cannot sit idle. A 120-unit bond, locked 10 epochs, loses 4% of face value each epoch; verified work alone restores it, and a quill-signed stamp records each refresh. Below 60 the identity is downgraded, loses rewards, and an onyx entry flags it for review. Forgery costs 50% of residual value plus a 6-epoch freeze, while a beacon audit samples 5% of bonds per epoch. For 1,000 clones the outlay is 120,000 units, depreciation drains 4,800 per epoch, and 10 idle epochs erase over 40,000 before any penalty.
